scenario: [LTAC.3.3] — an `after <dur>:` timer is asserted PLAINLY, not `emit ... logical`, so it carries no truth-maintenance link to the parent match and MUST survive the parent fact's retraction. Cancellation is only via `as`-keyed supersedure ([LTAC.2.2.1]), never parent-justification withdrawal. Pin: assert Trig (arms a 5_s timer on pump), RETRACT Trig before the delay elapses, advance past 5_s, pump — the after-body still fires and emits Delayed. The final fact_assert (Delayed) landing AFTER the parent's fact_retract is the proof the timer was not cancelled by the retract. The body emits a `ttl` Delayed because a `logical` emit in an `after` body is refused ([LLOG.11.9]).
rules_ds:
schema Trig scope logical:
    entity_id: String key

schema Delayed scope ttl 1_h:
    dummy: Int

rule delayed:
    Trig
->
    after 5_s:
        emit Delayed dummy: 0
